headline_marked: X Money [[launches in the US]] for Premium subscribers
headline: X Money launches in the US for Premium subscribers
summary: Elon Musk's payment platform offers a digital wallet, P2P payments, and a Visa card, now rolling out to X Premium and Premium Plus users.
details: X Money, a key component of Elon Musk's vision for X as an 'everything app,' has officially begun its rollout in the United States. Initially available to X Premium and Premium Plus subscribers, the platform aims to integrate financial services directly into the social media experience.

The service includes a digital wallet, peer-to-peer payment capabilities akin to Venmo, and a physical metal Visa card that can be customized with a user's X username. Users can also add X Money to their Apple Wallet for added convenience.

X Money advertises an Annual Percentage Yield (APY) of up to 6 percent. However, this top rate is exclusively for Premium Plus subscribers. Standard Premium users can achieve the same 6 percent APY by meeting certain deposit thresholds, earning them a 'boosted' rate.

This launch follows a period of invite-only beta testing and comes after Musk's earlier statements about bringing financial transactions to the platform. Concerns regarding consumer safety and financial stability have been raised by some regulators, but X is proceeding with its integration plans.

The platform offers free money transfers within X, further encouraging its use for everyday transactions. This move signifies X's ambition to broaden its functionality beyond social networking and into comprehensive digital services.

headline_marked: Microsoft unveils AI security tools [[outperforming competitors]]
headline: Microsoft unveils AI security tools outperforming competitors
summary: Microsoft's new AI security tools claim to be faster, cheaper, and more effective than existing solutions, aiming to combat the accelerating pace of cyberattacks.
details: Microsoft has launched new AI-powered security tools designed to help customers continuously identify and reduce their exposure to security risks. These tools are built on the company's MAI-Thinking-1 platform and are trained on vast amounts of security data from their extensive product patching and incident response experience.

The first tool, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, is specifically trained for software vulnerability analysis. It achieved a 96% score on the CyberGYM benchmark, outperforming models from Anthropic, Google Gemini, and OpenAI GPT by 12 points. This new offering also costs half as much as previous versions.

The second tool, Project Perception, utilizes specialized AI agents for red-, blue-, and green-team functions to find, investigate, and correct vulnerabilities. Microsoft states this platform can perform 90% of tasks at a lower cost than competitors, reserving more expensive alternatives for the remaining 10%.

These advancements come in response to the increasing speed and scale of AI-accelerated cyberattacks. Microsoft acknowledges that traditional security approaches are struggling to keep pace with emerging threats in complex digital environments.

While the tools are currently in preview and show promise, the recent OpenAI security model incident highlights the need for caution. The article suggests that while there are risks in adopting new AI security agents, the risks of not adopting them are also significant and present a complex balancing act for organizations.
caption:
Microsoft launches new AI security tools that reportedly outperform competitors like OpenAI and Google Gemini, while costing half as much.

Microsoft has launched new AI-powered security tools designed to help customers continuously identify and reduce their exposure to security risks. These tools are built on the company's MAI-Thinking-1 platform and are trained on vast amounts of security data from their extensive product patching and incident response experience.

The first tool, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, is specifically trained for software vulnerability analysis. It achieved a 96% score on the CyberGYM benchmark, outperforming models from Anthropic, Google Gemini, and OpenAI GPT by 12 points. This new offering also costs half as much as previous versions.

The second tool, Project Perception, utilizes specialized AI agents for red-, blue-, and green-team functions to find, investigate, and correct vulnerabilities. Microsoft states this platform can perform 90% of tasks at a lower cost than competitors, reserving more expensive alternatives for the remaining 10%.

These advancements come in response to the increasing speed and scale of AI-accelerated cyberattacks. Microsoft acknowledges that traditional security approaches are struggling to keep pace with emerging threats in complex digital environments.

While the tools are currently in preview and show promise, the recent OpenAI security model incident highlights the need for caution. The article suggests that while there are risks in adopting new AI security agents, the risks of not adopting them are also significant and present a complex balancing act for organizations.
